definition: A named, versioned value in Key Vault - typically a credential for a service that cannot use Entra ID, such as a payment provider's API key. Each secret should carry an expiry date and a rotation path. Key Vault also holds cryptographic keys and TLS certificates, which it can renew automatically.
example: payment-api-key in kv-shop-prod has an expiry date and is rotated by a function every 90 days.

definition: An App Service, Functions or Container Apps setting whose value points at a Key Vault secret. The platform resolves it with the app's managed identity and gives the code an ordinary environment variable, so the secret never appears in settings, pipelines or config files. A reference without a version follows the latest value, refreshed within a day or on restart.

A Key Vault setting that stops anyone - even an Owner - from permanently deleting a soft-deleted vault or object before its retention period ends. It cannot be turned off once enabled, and it is required before using a customer-managed key, because a purged key makes everything encrypted with it unreadable.
example: kv-shop-prod has purge protection, so an attacker with an admin token cannot destroy the key that encrypts the backups.

definition: Replacing a secret with a new value on a schedule or on demand, so a leaked value stops working quickly. On Azure, Key Vault raises a near-expiry event through Event Grid and a small function creates the new value; versionless references pick it up. Where a provider allows two keys, rotate them alternately so one is always valid.
example: Thirty days before payment-api-key expires, a function requests a new key and stores it as a new version.

definition: A central store for non-secret application settings and feature flags, shared by every service. Labels separate environments, snapshots record what was live at a release, and values can be Key Vault references resolved by each app with its own identity. Free tier for dev; Standard about $36 a month per store.
example: appcs-shop holds the API's timeouts and URLs under prod and dev labels, plus the NewCheckout feature flag.

definition: A named switch the code checks at run time to turn behaviour on or off, optionally for a percentage of users, named groups or a time window. It separates deploying code from releasing a feature, so a problem is fixed by flipping a switch rather than rolling back a deploy.
example: The new checkout is live for 10% of shoppers through the NewCheckout flag and can be switched off in seconds.
